ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a battery labeled 12 volts, and the battery is connected by wires to the terminal block on the right side. Above the terminal block, a resistor labeled 50 Ω can be seen, and beside it there is a Zener diode labeled Zener diode; below it is connected Motor. The resistor is located between the 12 V power supply and the load regulation node, and the motor and the 5 V Zener diode share this regulation node. Reasoning: The Zener diode clamps the load node at 5 V, therefore the voltage across the 50 Ω resistor is 12 V − 5 V = 7 V. The resistor current is Ires = 7 V / 50 Ω = 0.14 A = 140 mA. Given the motor current Imotor = 120 mA, according to the node current relationship, the Zener current Izener = 140 mA − 120 mA = 20 mA. The Zener diode power is Pzener = Vz × Izener = 5 V × 20 mA = 100 mW.

raw_record.question_text: Calculate the power dissipated by the 5-volt zener diode for the given motor current, assuming the battery voltage remains constant at 12 volts, as shown in the figure. Given \( I_\text{motor} = 120 \, \text{mA} \), the zener power \( P_\text{zener} \) is ______ mW.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify the 50 Ω resistor between the 12 V source and the regulated load node, with motor and zener sharing that node. From the text, take Vbattery = 12 V, Vz = 5 V, and Imotor = 120 mA. Since the zener clamps the load node to 5 V, the resistor voltage is 12 − 5 = 7 V, so Ires = 7/50 = 0.14 A = 140 mA. By KCL, Izener = Ires − Imotor = 140 − 120 = 20 mA. Then Pzener = 5 V × 20 mA = 100 mW.
